items.title: Show HN: I trained a 125M model to autocomplete piano on-device
items.excerpt: I trained a 125M-parameter transformer to autocomplete piano performances in real time (~108 notes/sec on an iPhone 15). The idea is basically GitHub Copilot or Tabnine, except instead of prompting it with code, you prompt it by playing a few notes on a MIDI piano. The model...

brief.whatHappened: "Show HN: I trained a 125M model to autocomplete piano on-device" reached the Hacker News front page with 598 points and 117 comments. The idea is basically GitHub Copilot or Tabnine, except instead of prompting it with code, you prompt it by playing a few notes on a MIDI piano.

items.title: Upcoming Next.js August Security Release
items.excerpt: Next.js is preparing a scheduled August security release for August 26, 2026.

brief.whatHappened: Next.js Blog published "Upcoming Next.js August Security Release". Next.js is preparing a scheduled August security release for August 26, 2026.
brief.whyItMatters: Understory and most of your client projects run on React and Next.js, so framework changes land directly in code you maintain.

keyConcepts.explanation: React components that render on the server and send their output, not their code, to the browser. Only interactive parts ship JavaScript.
Attaching event handlers to server-rendered HTML in the browser. Until it finishes the page is visible but not interactive.

brief.whatHappened: "The August 17 outage" reached the Hacker News front page with 643 points and 755 comments.
brief.whyItMatters: Failures at scale follow a small number of patterns. Each real incident or analysis is a worked example of a pattern you will meet in your own systems.

keyConcepts.explanation: A written account of an incident covering what happened, why the safeguards did not stop it, and what changes as a result.
Getting several machines to agree on one value or one order of events even when some of them fail or messages are lost.

items.title: The Pulse: We need to talk about migrations with AI
items.excerpt: Asana completed a testing framework migration in two weeks, that they would have delayed for years more, and they’re not alone. Also: AI startups could make Gartner much less relevant, and more

brief.whatHappened: The Pragmatic Engineer published "The Pulse: We need to talk about migrations with AI". Asana completed a testing framework migration in two weeks, that they would have delayed for years more, and they’re not alone. Also: AI startups could make Gartner much less relevant, and more
brief.whyItMatters: Most applications are limited by their database before anything else. Changes here reach schema design, query cost and how safely you can migrate.

keyConcepts.explanation: A versioned change to a database schema. Safe ones are split into steps so old and new application code both keep working.
A sorted structure that lets the database find rows without scanning the whole table. Each one speeds reads and slows writes.

brief.whyItMatters: A flaw found in someone else's stack is often present in yours. Reading the attack tells you which assumption to check in your own code.

keyConcepts.explanation: A public identifier for one specific vulnerability, so advisories, scanners and patches can refer to the same flaw.
A list of what you protect, who might attack it and where trust changes hands. It tells you which defences are worth building.
